name: Fabiola Agustina Kansil
title: Senior Principal Counsellor
bio: Fabiola is a highly experienced counselling professional whose career reflects a deep commitment to supporting individuals and communities across a range of complex issues. With years of work and practice in International School and Family Service Centre, she developed a strong foundation in community-based work, addressing diverse psychosocial and mental health concerns for people from all walks of life.

Since joining NUS in January 2013, Fabiola has played a pivotal role in shaping the development of student mental health services. She holds a Graduate Certificate in Clinical Supervision and recently completed a Group Supervision course, further strengthening her clinical expertise. She is a Registered Counsellor and Clinical Member of the Singapore Association for Counselling (SAC). Fabiola is also trained in EMDR Level 3 and Satir Model Level 2, besides other modalities, enabling her to work effectively with students facing a variety of therapeutic needs.

Fabiola has provided consultations since 2016, offering valuable clinical insights and guidance to her peers. Since 2022, she has expanded her impact as a clinical supervisor, fostering the growth and reflective practice of counsellors in the field. As a registered member of the Singapore Association for Counselling, she is committed to upholding the highest levels of ethical and professional practice and is actively working towards certification as an SAC Supervisor.

As Head overseeing NUS student mental health services, Fabiola has a comprehensive view of the evolving needs of the student population. She works closely with a wide array of stakeholders—including students, faculty, and external partners—to ensure that mental health support is accessible, evidence-based, and responsive.

name: Hema D/O Sivanathan
title: Senior Principal Counsellor
bio: Hema is a Lead Counsellor with over a decade of dedicated service across diverse settings, including forensic environments and educational institutions. Her broad clinical expertise encompasses supporting individuals navigating a wide spectrum of psychological challenges, such as stress, depression, anxiety, adjustment difficulties, attachment concerns, complex trauma, and interpersonal struggles.

As a member of HWB’s student-facing team at University Counselling Services (UCS), Hema delivers individual counselling while championing the cause of student mental health and well-being in NUS. She draws upon a robust foundation in evidence-based modalities—including Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT), mindfulness-based interventions, and Eye Movement Desensitisation and Reprocessing (EMDR).

A registered member of the Singapore Association for Counselling (SAC), Hema is actively advancing her professional journey towards SAC Supervisor membership and full EMDR certification. Since 2016, she has provided informal consultations to colleagues and, from 2022, has formally supervised clinicians, reflecting her deep commitment to nurturing the next generation of counsellors. Her advanced training includes a Graduate Certificate in Clinical Supervision, EMDR Level 3, and Brainspotting Level 1.

Hema’s supervisory approach is eclectic and integrative, weaving together multiple therapeutic frameworks and reflective practices. She is dedicated to fostering her supervisees’ clinical competence, encouraging self-reflection, and supporting their ongoing professional development, thus contributing meaningfully to the growth of the counselling profession.

name: Angeline Jayanthi
title: Senior Principal Counsellor
bio: Dr. Angeline Jayanthi is an experienced counselling professional with over a decade of clinical practice across diverse settings and client groups. She holds a Doctor of Professional Studies in Counselling and Psychotherapy and is currently Lead Counsellor at University Counselling Services, where she supports students facing academic, emotional, and personal challenges.

A Master Clinical Member and Registered Clinical Supervisor with the Singapore Association for Counselling, Angeline’s therapeutic approach is empathetic, culturally sensitive, and integrative, drawing on CBT, Schema Therapy, Internal Family Systems, EMDR Level 1, Gottman Couples Training Level 1 and various trauma focused modalities.

As a supervisor, she offers reflective, developmental guidance tailored to each clinician’s stage using the 7-Eyed model of supervision, with a strong focus on ethical practice, cultural competence, and professional growth. She prioritizes building a collaborative and trusting relationship with supervisees, fostering an environment where open dialogue, professional growth, and self-reflection are encouraged.

name: Evangeline Chen
title: Senior Counsellor
bio: Evangeline is a senior counsellor at UCS and Clinical Member of Singapore Association for Counselling (SAC). She currently supports students with a wide range of presenting concerns, including trauma, anxiety, depression, grief and relational issues. Her integrative therapeutic approach draws from Attachment-Focused Eye Movement Desensitisation and Reprocessing (AF-EMDR), Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT) and Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), tailored to each student’s needs.

Evangeline has been supporting colleagues through case consultations and clinical supervision since 2022 and 2024, respectively. She completed her Certificate in Clinical Supervision with Counselling and Care Centre (CCC) in 2024. Her supervision approach focuses on creating a safe and supportive environment, so as to grow in clinical competence and ability to reflect on their practice.

name: Benjamin Tan
title: Principal Counsellor
bio: Ben is a Counselling Psychologist by training, who completed his masters in the United States in 2013 and has been with NUS since 2017. He is a Registered Counsellor and Registered Clinical Supervisor with the Singapore Association for Counselling (SAC) so he is able to provide supervision for colleagues with SAC, but not SPS hours requirements under the current HWB internal supervision framework.

Ben's main theoretical orientation is Psychodynamic-Intersubjectivity, to which he has incorporated additional interventive skillsets such as Motivational Interviewing, Schema Therapy, AF-EMDR, Collaborative & Proactive Solutions, and the Gottman Couples method. His past clinical work experiences have included substance abuse / addiction work in tertiary education and hospital settings, systemic and behavioural work in a special needs school, as well as broad spectrum psychotherapy work with the Employee Assistance Program for a US state government. Ben is also comfortable working at the intersection of psychotherapy and spirituality, having also completed graduate studies in Pastoral Ministry concurrent with his psychology training.

At HWB, Ben's current clinical deployment within UCS is to himself conduct as well as support the broader team in delivering individual, couples, and group interventions as assigned. He also helps to coordinate matters related to critical incident and crisis response training and policies. To this end, he is also familiar with the principles and approaches of the NOVA crisis intervention framework and incorporates them into his work supporting clients as well as fellow HWB clinicians processing the clinical stressors of vicarious trauma, and transference reactions.

In terms of supervisory style, he prefers an affirming, collaborative, and strengths-based approach that starts with clear setting of joint hopes and goals, with ample space for adaptation and accommodating of changes, as needed, along the way. In previous supervision cycles he has supported colleagues with counselling and social work backgrounds, in addition to providing day-to-day case management, risk, clinical consultations for all types of clinicians within UCS. Ben's clinical supervision training (a Postgraduate Certificate in Clinical and Casework Supervision) was grounded in multi-modal and systemic thinking, reflexive practice, as well as affirming the Person of the Therapist.

As mentioned at the beginning of this blurb, Ben would be more suitable for supervisees needing SAC supervision hours, but is also open to support any colleagues interested to converse on matters sundry, be they clinical, psychological, vegetable, animal, or mineral.

name: Carol Chan
title: Senior Counsellor
bio: Carol is a Senior Counsellor with University Counselling Services (UCS) and has over 10 years of experience supporting university students through a wide range of personal, emotional, and psychological challenges. She holds a Master of Counselling and is a Registered Counsellor and Clinical Member of the Singapore Association for Counselling (SAC).

She works with individuals and couples, with a particular interest in supporting those who have experienced trauma. Her approach integrates Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR), Somatic Experiencing (SE), and Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT) to help clients process difficult experiences, strengthen resilience, and move toward healing and growth. She is also trained in the Gottman Method for Couple Counselling and group work interventions, and is currently working toward certification in Attachment-Focused Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (AF-EMDR).

In addition to her counselling practice, Carol provides clinical consultation and supervision. She holds a Post Graduate Certificate in Clinical and Casework Supervision from Counselling and Care Centre.

Carol is committed to creating a safe, compassionate, and non-judgmental space where students feel heard, understood, and supported as they navigate life's challenges and work toward greater wellbeing.

name: Valerie Chua
title: Senior Counselling Psychologist
bio: Valerie is a Counselling Psychologist with a decade of experience across diverse settings, including community services, educational institutions, and forensic setting. She has supported individuals facing a broad spectrum of psychological challenges such as depression, anxiety, psychosis, trauma, stress and burnout, interpersonal difficulties, and adjustment-related concerns.

She is currently part of the University Counselling Services team at NUS, where she provides both individual and group-based psychological support to students. Valerie integrates a range of therapeutic modalities in her practice, including Cognitive Behavioural Therapy, Schema Therapy, and Mindfulness-based Interventions, tailoring her approach to meet the unique needs of each client.
Valerie is a member of the Singapore Psychological Society and completed a postgraduate certification in clinical supervision in 2025.

Valerie’s beliefs about supervision are grounded in the importance of thoughtful reflection and the cultivation of self-awareness. She views supervision as a collaborative and supportive space that not only enhances clinical skills and ethical decision-making but also fosters personal and professional growth.

name: Mandy Lee
title: Principal Counsellor
bio: Mandy is a practicing counsellor with over a decade of experience in the mental health field. Her career has afforded her the opportunity to work with diverse populations across various settings, including hospitalization programs and private practice.

Before transitioning into counselling, Mandy began her professional journey in corporate communications, where she developed strong skills in active listening and relationship-building; strengths that continue to inform her work as a mental health professional today.

Mandy believes that life often brings complex challenges, and her role as a therapist is to support individuals in navigating these difficulties and developing effective, positive coping strategies. Her therapeutic approach is grounded in evidence-based modalities, including Cognitive Behaviour Therapy (CBT), Schema Therapy, and Internal Family Systems (IFS). Recently, she has also incorporated Emotional Freedom Technique (EFT) - a form of tapping on specific meridian points while focusing on negative emotions as a complementary tool for the populations she serves.

Mandy is a registered supervisor with the Singapore Association for Counselling (SAC). She believes that the supervisory relationship should be built on a foundation of trust, non-judgment, and acceptance. Mandy is committed to supporting the clinical development of her supervisees while emphasizing the importance of cultivating self-awareness and a grounded therapeutic presence. Above all, she strives to create a safe, supportive environment where supervisees can grow both personally and professionally.

name: Joanna Tan
title: Head, NUS Care Unit & Clinical Governance Lead (Senior Principal Clinical Psychologist)
bio: Joanna is a Clinical Psychologist with over a decade of experience across public, private, and educational mental health settings. Her training spans the United States, Australia, and Singapore, and she has worked with individuals across the lifespan—from young children to older adults—presenting with a broad spectrum of psychological and psychiatric concerns.

Her clinical career has included working with both inpatient and outpatient populations in general psychiatry, as well as with children and adolescents experiencing mood and anxiety difficulties. Most recently, Joanna served at Yale-NUS College supporting young adults navigating complex developmental, relational, and emotional challenges.

Alongside clinical work, Joanna is a registered psychologist and SRP-approved supervisor who has been providing clinical supervision for the past ten years. She has supervised trainees from a variety of postgraduate Clinical Psychology and Counselling programs.

Joanna is trained in a range of therapeutic modalities—including Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT), Emotion-Focused Therapy (EFT), and Schema Therapy—but her core orientation, both as a therapist and supervisor, is grounded in psychodynamic psychotherapy.

Her supervisory style is relational, reflective, and insight-focused. She offers a psychologically safe and attuned space for supervisees to explore the emotional dimensions of their clinical work, navigate transference and countertransference, and reflect on their own professional identity development. Through a psychodynamic lens, Joanna supports supervisees in deepening their understanding of client dynamics, while encouraging growth in their own self-awareness and therapeutic presence.

name: Soon Jiaying
title: Senior Wellbeing Specialist Partner (Principal Clinical Psychologist)
bio: Jiaying is a Clinical Psychologist with experience across various settings, including special education, community services, primary care, and private healthcare. She has worked with individuals facing a wide range of psychological concerns such as stress, depression, anxiety, adjustment difficulties, relationship challenges, parenting issues, and experiences of grief and loss.

Currently, Jiaying is part of HWB’s Staff Wellbeing and Engagement team, where she provides individual psychotherapeutic support to NUS staff. She draws from a range of evidence-based therapeutic approaches, including Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT), Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), Solution-Focused Therapy (SFT), and Mindfulness-based interventions.

Jiaying is an SRP-approved Supervisor and has been offering clinical supervision for the past three years. Her training includes a Certificate of Attainment in Supervision, as well as formal knowledge in Reflective Practice and Deliberate Practice in Supervision.

Jiaying’s supervision is grounded in relationship-building and thoughtful reflection. She values collaboration and is committed to supporting her supervisees in deepening their understanding of client dynamics, while fostering growth in self-awareness and therapeutic presence.

name: Dominic Yeo
title: Senior Care Manager
suitableFor: Case Manager, Care Manager, Residential Wellbeing Manager
bio: Dominic holds a Bachelor's degree in Social Work and has had the privilege of working in both social service agencies and the Ministry of Health in the past. Due to these roles, his training and experience range from case management and counselling to mental health policy and administration. Dominic enjoys working with individuals and families navigating safety and risk concerns, and he leans on psychodynamic, person-centred and CBT approaches to guide his practice.

Dominic has also been supervising students and social workers for 4 years; a role he finds deeply rewarding and meaningful. His supervisory style is warm and nurturing, always centred on the supervisee’s learning needs and growth. Past supervisees have described the supervision space as safe, validating, and reflective, where honest, constructive feedback supported their growth in skill and confidence.

name: Kirsty Png
title: Senior Wellbeing Specialist Partner (Senior Counselling Psychologist)
bio: Kirsty is a Senior Wellbeing Specialist Partner with HWB. As an SRP approved supervisor, her clinical experience spans across a range of presenting concerns including trauma, grief and loss, mood & anxiety disorders, learning needs, parenting challenges, and relationship challenges.

With professional training in Counselling Psychology, Educational Therapy, and Gottman Couples Therapy level 3, Kirsty has worked in the educational, community, public hospital & private health care settings. Kirsty adopts an integrative approach which encompasses Psychodynamic, SBT, DBT, SFBT, MI, Gottman Couples Therapy, and TFCBT modalities.
Supervisory style wise, Kirsty holds space for reflective and collaborative practices, placing much value in scaffolding supervisee’s growth as a person as well as in professional capacities.

name: Jaya Rajesh
title: Senior Residential Wellbeing Manager
suitableFor: Case Manager, Care Manager, Residential Wellbeing Manager
bio: Jaya is a dedicated Residential Wellness Manager with over 11 years of experience in providing clinical supervision. She holds master’s degrees in Social Work, Narrative Therapy, and Community Work, and is a registered SASW supervisor. Jaya has supervised social work interns since 2014 and junior staff from 2016 to 2022, offering both group and individual supervision. Her expertise lies in utilizing social work principles, case management, and narrative therapy to support and empower those under her care. Since 2024, Jaya has also been offering clinical supervision within HWB, guiding practitioners in their professional development and ensuring high standards of clinical practice. She is passionate about helping individuals re-author their stories, guiding them through personal challenges with empathy and a strengths-based approach.

In her current role, Jaya focuses on addressing the emotional and psychological concerns of residential students, offering timely guidance and support to ensure their well-being. She is also actively involved in the development of student leaders, conducting training sessions, and organizing various engagement activities to foster a connected and supportive residential community. Through her holistic and compassionate approach, Jaya creates a nurturing environment that enables students to thrive both personally and academically.

name: Goh Zhengqin
title: Deputy Director & Deputy Head (Senior Principal Clinical Psychologist)
bio: Zheng is a Clinical Psychologist with 15 years of experience in tertiary public mental health that included forensic work, and in tertiary educational settings. He has worked with individuals presenting with mood and anxiety disorders, anger issues, trauma, OCD, psychotic disorders, paraphilias, and experiences of grief and loss.

He has been an expert witness in court on several occasions. He draws from a variety of evidence-based therapeutic approaches including Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT), Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), Eye Movement Desensitisation and Reprocessing (EMDR), Solution-Focused Therapy (SFT), and Motivational Interviewing (MI), and takes an eclectic and personalised approach with each client.
Zheng’s approach to supervision is supervisee-centric, focused on relationship-building, reflexivity, and tailored to the needs of the supervisee at each point of consultation.

name: Muhamad Haikel
title: Head, Staff Wellbeing & Engagement (Senior Care Manager)
suitableFor: Case Manager, Care Manager, Residential Wellbeing Manager
bio: Haikel began his career at NUS Health and Wellbeing (HWB) as a Care Manager, where he provided care management support to staff respondents and employees experiencing mental health challenges, facilitating their reintegration into the workplace. He brings over seven years of case management experience, having had the privilege of working with adults and seniors across the humanitarian, social service, and community care sectors. His practice is grounded in humanistic, person-centred, and restorative approaches.

A strong advocate for lifelong learning, Haikel is currently pursuing Korean Language for fun. He also holds a Master of Counselling with a specialisation in Couples and Family Therapy, Postgraduate Diploma in Counselling Psychology, Graduate Diploma in Applied Positive Psychology, Bachelor of Social Work, and Diploma in Nursing.

In addition to his clinical background, Haikel is an experienced Learning and Development (L&D) practitioner. He has trained, mentored, and supported aspiring adult educators across all levels, from foundational to master trainer certification. He is proficient in designing and delivering mental health and psychosocial support training programmes, particularly in psychological first aid (PFA) and peer support, using a train-the-trainer model.

In clinical supervision, Haikel integrates the Common Factors and parallel process of the Person-of-the-Supervisor (POTS) and Person-of-the-Therapist (POTT) supervision models with adult learning principles. He tailors his supervisory approach according to the supervisee's developmental stage, focusing on their strengths and growth potential. He is committed to fostering reflective and reflexive practice in a psychologically safe environment, offering a supervision experience that is humanistic, person-centred, and nurturing. Haikel values authenticity, transparent communication, proactiveness, and self-directed learning in the supervisory relationship.

Haikel currently serves as the Head of Staff Wellbeing and Engagement at NUS, where he oversees staff mental health services. His professional interests include suicidology, disaster mental health, and crisis management. He aspires to become a couples therapist and a practitioner-educator.

With his breadth of experience, Haikel is well-suited to supervisees seeking guidance in case management or those exploring careers in mental health, particularly in social work, counselling, or psychology. While he possesses over four years of social work experience, he is not accredited with the Social Work Accreditation and Advisory Board (SWAAB), which does not allow him to provide supervision for professionals needing to clock accredited social work supervision hours.

name: Adrian Wan
title: Senior Residential Wellbeing Manager
suitableFor: Case Manager, Care Manager, Residential Wellbeing Manager
bio: Adrian holds a Master's degree in Counselling and a Certificate in Supervision for Professionals, and brings over 30 years of professional experience across people-focused roles. He has spent more than six years supporting students at NUS, journeying with them through a range of personal, academic, developmental, and wellbeing-related challenges.

As a Clinical Supervisor, he seeks to create a safe, collaborative, and reflective space where supervisees can strengthen their clinical competencies, deepen their self-awareness, and grow in confidence as practitioners. He believes effective supervision extends beyond case discussions to include critical reflection, ethical practice, and professional development.

His supervision approach is developmental and strengths-based, recognising that each supervisee brings unique experiences, capabilities, and learning needs. Through a balance of support, constructive challenge, and encouragement, he aims to help supervisees build on their strengths, navigate clinical complexities, and develop their own professional identity and counselling style.
He welcomes opportunities to work with helping professionals seeking a supportive, reflective, and growth-oriented supervision experience.

name: Jasmin Foong
title: Senior Residential Wellbeing Manager
suitableFor: Case Manager, Care Manager, Residential Wellbeing Manager
bio: Jasmin is a social worker by training and holds a Master's degree in Social Work, as well as a postgraduate diploma in Systemic Family Psychotherapy from Counselling and Care Centre. She is currently a Senior Residential Wellness Manager, supporting students living in hostels through reintegration work and outreach.

With 15 years of experience, Jasmin has mainly worked in the medical setting, supporting individuals with a range of psychological concerns, including anxiety, depression, and other psychiatric conditions. Her experience also includes working with people living with HIV, as well as teenagers with eating disorders and their families.

In her clinical practice and supervision, Jasmin draws primarily on systemic ideas. She sees supervision as a collaborative process of co-creating ideas and a safe space to support ethical decision-making, client empowerment, reflexive practice, and the development of the self of the worker.
Jasmin is a registered practitioner with the Singapore Association of Social Workers.

name: Carissa Yenn
title: Senior Clinical Psychologist
bio: Carissa is a registered clinical psychologist with UCS, where she has been supporting students through psychotherapy and assessments since 2022. She draws from a range of therapeutic approaches in her practice, including Schema Therapy and Emotion Focused Therapy. She attended the SPS Competency Based Supervision training in 2026, which marked the beginning of a humbling journey of growing to be a clinical supervisor.

name: Shatish Jayakumar Rajamanickam
title: Senior Counsellor
bio: Shathish is a counsellor with close to a decade of experience across both local and international settings. For the past five years, he has been a member of the University Counselling Services team at the National University of Singapore (NUS), where he provides psychological support to students.

He has worked with individuals facing a wide range of psychological concerns, including anxiety, depression, interpersonal, adjustment, stress, and burnout. Shathish draws from a variety of therapeutic modalities in his clinical practice, including Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT), Schema Therapy, Internal Family Systems Therapy (IFS), and a range of Mindfulness-based interventions, which he tailors to suit each client’s unique needs.

He is a member of the Singapore Association for Counselling and is in the process of completing his registration. As part of his ongoing professional development, he will also be undergoing training in clinical supervision. Shathish views supervision as a safe, supportive environment that goes beyond enhancing clinical skills by also encouraging personal and professional growth.
